nodes.name: In Situ Self-Assembly of Ni-Fe LDH (Nitrate)
nodes.procedure: The fabrication of 3D Ni-Fe LDH/IF(NO3-) was accomplished by immersing the clean iron foam (IF) in a solution of Ni(NO3)2 at room temperature without other energy input. The Fe foam is redox-etched by Ni2+ through a single displacement reaction, and generated Fe2+ is oxidized to Fe3+ and OH- via oxygen reduction, followed by coprecipitation into LDH nanosheets.

nodes.characterization_summary: ICP analysis corroborated the Fe-Ni molar ratios as 3.5:6.5 (NO3-), 4.6:5.4 (SO42-), and 5.2:4.8 (Cl-).
nodes.evidence_snippet: inductively coupled plasma (ICP) analysis corroborated that the Fe-Ni molar ratio was 3.5:6.5, 4.6:5.4, 5.2:4.8 (Table 1).

nodes.characterization_summary: SEM showed iron foam fully covered by densely packed Ni-Fe LDH nanosheets with diameters around 500 nm and thicknesses of 20 nm.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The SEM images (Figure 2a,b) showed that the iron foam was fully covered by the densely packed Ni-Fe LDH nanosheets. The diameter and thickness of this nanosheet is about 500 and 20 nm

nodes.characterization_summary: TEM confirmed a clear nanosheet structure for the Ni-Fe LDH materials.
nodes.evidence_snippet: it was further confirmed by TEM images (Figure 2c,d) exhibiting a clear nanosheet structure.

nodes.characterization_summary: XRD confirmed the formation of Ni-Fe LDH; the (003) reflection peak shifted from 11.9 to 11.1 degrees as anions changed from Cl- to SO4 2- and NO3-, indicating changing lattice distances.
nodes.evidence_snippet: XRD, which clearly implicates successful formation of Ni-Fe LDH on Fe foam (Figure 3a). ... the (003) reflection peak slightly shifts from 11.9 to 11.1 ... implying that different anions were embedded into the interlayer

nodes.characterization_summary: XPS confirmed Ni2+ (peaks at 855.4 and 873.0 eV) and Fe3+ (peaks at 711.5 and 724.8 eV) in the Ni-Fe LDH.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Binding energy peaks at 855.4 and 873.0 eV were ascribed to Ni 2+ 2p 3/2 and Ni 2+ 2p 1/2 ... peaks located at 711.5 and 724.8 eV ... assigned to Fe 2p 3/2 and Fe 2p 1/2 ... existence of Fe 3+

nodes.characterization_summary: Double-layer capacitance (Cdl) measurements showed all Ni-Fe LDHs have higher surface areas than bare IF, with the NO3- variant having the smallest Cdl among the LDHs due to thicker nanosheets.
nodes.evidence_snippet: ECSA ... evaluated by measuring the electrochemical double-layer capacitance (Cdl). ... although the catalytic performance of Ni-Fe LDH/IF (NO3-) is the best, we found that its Cdl is the smallest.

properties.observation: Shows the electrochemical activity (likely Oxygen Evolution Reaction) of the tested materials. Ni-Fe LDH/IF samples show significantly higher activity than bare Iron foam. Activity order: NO₃⁻ > Cl⁻ > SO₄²⁻.

nodes.characterization_summary: Stability tests showed that all three Ni-Fe LDH electrodes maintain their catalytic current for at least 10 hours without significant decline.
nodes.evidence_snippet: all of these NiFe LDH/IF electrodes can maintain its catalytic current density for 10 h at least without obvious declining under the operating voltage.

properties.observation: The plot shows the potential stability of the three different Ni-Fe LDH/IF electrodes over a period of about 11 hours. Ni-Fe LDH/IF (NO₃⁻) operates at the lowest potential, followed by Ni-Fe LDH/IF (Cl⁻), and then Ni-Fe LDH/IF (SO₄²⁻). All samples show a slight increase in potential over time.

properties.description: A multi-step chronopotentiometry plot showing the potential response over time for three different materials. The potential increases in steps, likely corresponding to increases in applied current density.
properties.trend: At any given time/step, the operating potential follows the order: Ni-Fe LDH/IF (SO4 2-) > Ni-Fe LDH/IF (Cl-) > Ni-Fe LDH/IF (NO3-).

nodes.characterization_summary: Gas chromatography and optical probe measurements confirmed a Faradic efficiency close to 100% for oxygen evolution.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The generated oxygen was first confirmed by gas chromatography (GC) and then the faradic efficiency (FE) ... suggests a close to 100% FE, as shown in Figure 5.
